question: Which structure serves as the primary natural pacemaker of a healthy human heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial node fires impulses at the highest rate in the heart, making it the dominant natural pacemaker. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why is the short delay of the electrical impulse at the atrioventricular node important for heart function?

options.A: It stops electrical signals from traveling backward into the atria
options.B: It gives the ventricles enough time to fill completely with blood
options.C: It protects the delicate Purkinje fibers from electrical overload
options.D: It speeds up the heartbeat during times of physical stress

explanation: The pause at the AV node ensures the atria finish contracting and emptying their blood into the ventricles before ventricular contraction begins. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which ion rushing rapidly into the cardiac cell causes depolarization?
explanation: Rapid influx of positive sodium ions depolarizes the cell membrane, shifting the interior from negative to positive. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h2)

question: What happens to the electrical charge inside a cardiac cell during repolarization?

options.A: It stays balanced with zero electrical charge
options.D: It returns to a negative resting state

explanation: Repolarization restores the original negative resting membrane potential so the cell is ready for the next heartbeat. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h2)

question: What does a standard electrocardiogram (ECG) primarily measure?

options.A: Volume of blood pumped per minute
options.D: Oxygen saturation of the coronary blood

explanation: An ECG records the electrical signals produced by the heart muscle during depolarization and repolarization. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h3)

question: How do electrical signals from the deep heart muscle reach the electrodes attached to a patient's skin?

options.A: Special nerve fibers carry the signals directly to the electrode patches
options.B: The ECG machine generates magnetic fields that pull signals through the ribs
options.C: Blood cells physically transport the electrical charge to the surface
options.D: Body tissues conduct the electrical currents outward to the skin

explanation: Body fluids and tissues act as electrical conductors, allowing currents from the myocardium to reach skin-level electrodes. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h3)

question: Which part of the normal ECG waveform represents atrial depolarization?
explanation: The P wave shows the electrical wave sweeping across the atria, causing them to contract. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is the QRS complex much taller and sharper than the P wave on an ECG recording?

options.A: Electrical signals travel much faster through the ventricles than the atria
options.B: Electrodes are placed much closer to the ventricles on the chest
options.C: The ventricles contain vastly more muscle mass than the atria
options.D: The QRS complex records repolarization instead of depolarization

explanation: Larger muscle mass generates a stronger electrical voltage, resulting in a taller and more prominent QRS waveform. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h4)

question: How much time is represented by a single small horizontal box on standard ECG grid paper?
explanation: At a standard paper speed of 25 mm/s, each 1 mm small box horizontally equals 0.04 seconds. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h5)

question: What does an individual ECG "lead" actually represent during a 12-lead recording?

options.A: A distinct pathway through the atrioventricular node
options.B: A physical copper wire connected to a specific rib
options.C: The total electrical output of a single heart valve
options.D: A specific electrical viewing angle of the heart

explanation: Leads are mathematical or electrode combinations that view electrical currents from different geometric directions. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h5)

question: How can a nurse quickly estimate the ventricular rate from a 6-second ECG rhythm strip?

options.A: Count the number of R waves and multiply by 10
options.B: Add the height of all T waves together and divide by 2
options.C: Count the total number of small boxes and divide by 6
options.D: Count the P waves in 3 seconds and multiply by 30

explanation: Because a standard rhythm strip length of 6 seconds represents one-tenth of a minute, multiplying R waves by 10 gives the beats per minute. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is considered the normal duration range for a healthy PR interval?
explanation: A normal PR interval spans 3 to 5 small boxes, which equals 0.12 to 0.20 seconds of conduction time. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why is it important to remove skin oils and clip excessive chest hair before attaching ECG electrodes?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing a mild electrical shock
options.B: To allow the underlying lung sounds to be heard more clearly
options.C: To ensure firm adhesion and reduce electrical resistance for a clear tracing
options.D: To stop the patient from sweating during the recording process

explanation: Clean skin and solid contact minimize electrical interference and prevent artifact on the printed ECG strip. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h7)

question: Which of the following actions should the nurse instruct the patient to take during the active recording of a 12-lead ECG?

options.A: Take deep breaths and hold them tightly
options.B: Sit upright with both arms raised high
options.D: Lie completely still and avoid talking

explanation: Skeletal muscle movement from talking or shivering creates electrical artifact that mimics abnormal heart rhythms. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T11#BMP111_U5_T11_h7)
